jobs.title: GTM AI Lead
jobs.jd_full:
About Us

Every physical product you touch starts with raw materials & chemicals that someone has to find, qualify, and buy. The soap you wash your hands with, the laptop you’re looking at right now, and even the concrete sidewalk under your feet. That’s a $6T industry. Most of it still runs on spreadsheets, phone calls, and trade shows.

Valdera is the leading AI platform for chemicals and raw materials. Our agents help procurement teams find savings, reduce supply risk, and source from qualified suppliers. We also help suppliers find and win the right customers. We work with some of the largest manufacturers in the world, including market leaders in pharma, personal care, beauty, and industrials. Many of them spend $1B to $10B each on raw materials. They rely on Valdera as their source of truth and to run big workflows end to end.

Index Ventures led our $15M Series A, and we’re growing fast.

What's interesting?

You'll think like a product manager and own results like a revenue leader.

  • Drive real revenue - We're the fastest-growing company in our space, and we're investing heavily in technology to make step changes in how fast we sell. What you build shows up directly in our growth.
  • Build on a winning product - The largest manufacturers in the world rely on Valdera to run big purchasing and supply chain workflows end to end. Your work helps us win more of them, faster.
  • Have creative ownership - You'll help set the vision and have ownership of how we get there.
  • Work directly with the founders. You'll partner with them every week on how we sell, serve customers, and grow.
  • Build for top talent. Our people are technology-first and highly capable. You won't have to convince anyone to try what you build.
  • A fast engineering team. Our engineers are exceptional, and they'll speed you up instead of slowing you down.
  • You get the best tools. You'll have the budget to pick the best AI tools and data for the job.

Role Description

We're hiring our first GTM AI & Engineering Lead to keep accelerating Valdera's growth. You'll design the AI workflows our sales team runs on. Then you'll help build them.

Our AEs sell to some of the largest manufacturers in the world. Every deal takes deep account research, sharp meeting prep, tailored proposals, and steady follow-through. You'll build AI agents and workflows that handle that work, so our sellers spend their time with customers.

You'll start with sales and extend to customer success, forward deployed engineering, and marketing. You'll learn how each team works, where their time goes, and what would change their results. Then you'll prototype, prove ideas with data, and partner with our engineers to put it into production.

Role Responsibilities

  • Help set the AI vision for GTM. Decide which AI workflows, tools, and data will make the biggest step change in how fast we grow. Turn that into a plan the team believes in.
  • Learn how our sellers work. Sit with our AEs, CSMs, and FDEs. Map their workflows, find where their time goes, and pick the changes that will move results most.
  • Raise the bar for sales. Work with sales leaders as a peer. Challenge how we sell today, show them what's possible, and redesign the process around it.
  • Build AI agents for every stage of the deal. Automate account research, prospecting, meeting prep, call follow-ups, and proposals for Fortune 500 manufacturers. Every AE should have an AI team behind them.
  • Turn signals into pipeline. Use data from our platforms and from massive live global data sources to find the right accounts and the right moment to reach them, on both the buyer and supplier side.
  • Design how our systems fit together. Decide how Attio, our AI tools, and our data sources connect, from data models to integrations. Use AI to keep data clean, and make sure every tool earns its place.
  • Prototype fast. Build working versions with LLMs, coding agents, APIs, and automation tools. Test them with the team and keep what works.
  • Ship with engineering. Partner with our engineers to turn your best prototypes into production systems the whole team relies on.
  • Be data drive. Query and analyze pipeline, usage, and customer data. Judge every workflow by what it does to win rates, deal speed, and expansion.
  • Run AI the team can trust. Set guardrails, check output quality, and manage model costs as the agents scale.
  • Make change stick. Roll out each new workflow, train the team, and track adoption. A workflow only counts when people use it.

Experience & Qualifications

  • You have 5+ years in GTM engineering, revenue operations, sales, growth, BizOps, or product, ideally at a fast-growing B2B startup.
  • You've built AI workflows that a sales team uses every day. You can show what they did for revenue, pipeline, win rates, or time saved.
  • You've enabled cross-functional GTM teams before. Sales, customer success, and marketing moved faster because of what you built.
  • You think like a product manager. You start with the user's workflow and the outcome, then decide what to build.
  • You think in systems. You understand APIs, data schemas, and integration patterns, and you know how tools like CRMs, Claude, and Jira connect.
  • You're data driven. You can write queries, analyze data, and let real evidence drive your decisions.
  • You know how B2B sales works. You understand prospecting, long enterprise sales cycles, and how pipeline, win rates, and expansion drive growth.
  • You build your own prototypes with LLMs, coding agents, APIs, and automation tools.
  • You've partnered with engineers to take a prototype to production.
  • You love open-ended problems. You take a high-level goal, shape the plan, and see it through.

Our Culture

The best want to work with the best. That's why we obsess over our culture and bring in exceptional people to lead every part of the business. Above all, we look for curiosity. Our people ask the right questions, get to innovative answers, and do whatever it takes to win. Building a winning startup takes hard work and a lot of time together, so being low-ego, genuine, and fun matters just as much.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Fulfilment
jobs.jd_full:
About Nivoda

Nivoda is the operating system for the global jewellery industry. Our marketplace connects jewellers with suppliers of diamonds, gemstones, melee and finished jewellery in 70+ countries, with more than $300M in annual transactions and a $350B industry still waiting to be modernised. We are scaling fast, and we are only getting started.

Our Mission

For decades, the diamond trade has been slow, opaque and inefficient: hard to find stock, hard to trust prices, hard to know when anything will arrive. Nivoda exists to change that. We give businesses of every size, in every location, the same access to inventory, the same transparent pricing and the same reliable delivery as the biggest players in the industry.

The Fulfilment & Express Team

The Fulfilment & Express team is where Nivoda's promise to buyers is kept. We own how an order travels from supplier to jeweller: the delivery date we promise, the hubs that hold and check stock, the carriers that move it, and the returns and quality checks that protect every purchase. We are a remote-first team of product, engineering, design and QA who work closely with Operations, Customer Support, Sales and Supplier Experience. We are low on hierarchy and high on ownership, and we like solving problems where software meets the physical world.

About the Role

As our Senior Product Manager for Fulfilment & Express, you will own how Nivoda orders get from supplier to jeweller: accurately promised, reliably tracked and delivered fast. You will set the strategy and roadmap for a complex, operationally heavy product area that spans diamonds, gemstones, melee and finished jewellery, with physical hubs, carriers and suppliers behind every screen. Your work decides whether a jeweller trusts Nivoda with their next order, so this is a role with real commercial impact and plenty of room to lead.

What would YOU be doing?

  • Setting the fulfilment strategy for the next 2 to 4 quarters, making trade-offs explicit, including what we are choosing not to do and why

  • Owning the roadmap and the numbers: running quarterly planning, sizing opportunities and setting targets for delivery-as-promised, delivery date accuracy and delivery speed

  • Making our Promised Delivery Dates trustworthy by rolling out SLA-based, dynamic delivery dates across every category and route, and shaping how they are used for delay communications and, in time, shown to buyers

  • Scaling Express, our hub-based fast-delivery offer, including hub workflows (receiving, inventory and RFID put/pick, QC and dispatch), ready-to-wear jewellery, consignment flows and speed options such as same-day pickup

  • Owning jewellery returns and on-platform QC, from the manufacturer through to the hub, including hallmarking and consignment returns to suppliers

  • Improving the delivery experience through carrier and rate/transit integrations, consolidation, last-mile cost and efficiency, and clear order visibility for buyers

  • Translating hub operations, carrier behaviour, customs and supplier handling into clear product requirements, designing for the exceptions as much as the happy path

  • Turning support tickets, delay breaches, supplier performance data and customer feedback into prioritised problems, then deciding what to build, buy or fix operationally

  • Partnering daily with Engineering and Design, and closely with Operations, Customer Support, Account Management, Sales, Supplier Experience and Fintech so delivery, credit and payments feel like one journey for the buyer

  • Writing sharp PRDs and decision records, and reporting progress openly through our weekly updates

  • Mentoring other product managers and designers on working in operationally complex domains

What do we need from YOU?

  • 5 to 8 years in product management, including experience owning a complex product area end to end

  • Experience in fulfilment, logistics, supply chain or other operations-heavy products. You are comfortable where software meets warehouses, carriers, SLAs and customs

  • Strong systems thinking: you can map a multi-party process, find where promises break, and design for failure modes, delays and edge cases

  • Data fluency: you define the right metrics, query and interrogate data yourself (Snowflake, Mixpanel or similar) and use it to decide what to build next

  • Sound prioritisation and commercial judgement: you weigh impact, effort and risk honestly, say no clearly, and can explain the return on a fulfilment investment to leadership

  • Excellent cross-functional leadership: you build trust with engineers, operators and commercial teams, and influence without authority across time zones

  • Clear written communication: concise PRDs, roadmaps and updates that make decisions easy

  • Customer and operator empathy, and high agency: you spend time with jewellers, support teams and hub operators, you take ownership, and you follow things through to the outcome

Nice to have

  • Jewellery, diamond or luxury goods experience

  • Marketplace or B2B commerce experience, ideally two-sided with supply and demand constraints

  • Experience with carrier or shipping APIs, rate and transit tools, 3PL integrations, inventory systems or RFID

  • Experience building predictive or SLA-based estimates, such as delivery dates or ETAs

  • Experience with cross-border shipping, customs, duties or compliance (for example hallmarking and HS codes)

Our culture and what we offer

Nivoda is collaborative, high-growth and built on empowerment. You will have real ownership from day one, a team that wants you to succeed, and the chance to keep learning as the company scales. We are remote-first with flexible hours, and we trust you to do your best work your way.

Our current benefits

  • ⏰ Flexible working hours and a vibrant company culture

  • 🏡 Remote work

  • 🩺 Private health insurance

  • 📚 Opportunities for growth and learning

  • 💳 Flexible compensation card (meals, transport, childcare)

  • 🌴 Unlimited holiday allowance

  • 🚀 The chance to join during an exponential expansion phase

Equal opportunity

Nivoda is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team, and we welcome applications from everyone. Even if you do not meet 100% of our musts, do not let it stop you. If this role excites you, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.jd_full:
Company Overview

Deepgram is bringing the world’s most natural interface, voice, to the technology we use every day. More than 650,000 developers have used Deepgram to process more than 200,000 years of audio. Every day, more of the world’s conversations with AI run on our models.

Operating Principles

Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:

  1. Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.

  2. Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.

  3. Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.

  4. Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.

We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.

AI-First by Default

We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.

That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:

  • Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.

  • Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.

  • Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.

  • Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.

We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment.

THE ROLE

Director of Specialty Fibers

This role ensures that every product made from cashmere, merino, yak, alpaca, and other luxury fibers meets Quince's uncompromising standards for quality, sustainability, and affordability.

The Director blends deep technical expertise in fiber science with strategic supply chain leadership and cross-functional collaboration, serving as the central hub connecting sourcing, production, quality, and design teams across global markets.

Strategic Leadership & Supply Chain Management

Sourcing & Supplier Development

Quality Assurance & Technical Optimization

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, User Acquisition
jobs.jd_full:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile.

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $16B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 150+ people across 25+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance.

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.

The Role

As Senior Product Manager, User Acquisition, you'll explore an important extension of how RevenueCat helps developers grow: helping them not just monetize the users they have, but acquire more of the right users in the first place.

RevenueCat already has several footholds in user acquisition, including our Apple Ads integration and integrations across the attribution and MMP ecosystem. But we're still early in defining what a broader RevenueCat user acquisition product should become. You'll be the first dedicated product hire focused on this space, reporting directly to our product lead for Ads, with significant latitude to shape both the strategy and the products we build.

This is a genuine zero-to-one role. You won't inherit a predetermined roadmap. Your job will be to deeply understand how app developers acquire users today, identify where RevenueCat has an opportunity to solve problems meaningfully better, and turn those insights into products we can test, ship, and scale.

You'll bring real expertise in mobile performance marketing and user acquisition to that process. The opportunity could eventually span attribution and measurement, products built on top of existing acquisition channels, new ways to optimize spend using downstream monetization data, partnerships, advertising infrastructure, or things we haven't considered yet. We have hypotheses, but we're hiring you in part because we want your perspective on which ones are worth pursuing.

RevenueCat has some unusual advantages to build from: relationships with a large ecosystem of app developers, deep visibility into subscription and monetization outcomes, infrastructure already embedded in apps, and a growing advertising business. The challenge is figuring out how those assets can translate into something uniquely valuable for developers trying to grow.

About you:

  • You have 5+ years of experience owning meaningful product or growth decisions end-to-end. Your title may have been Product Manager, founder, growth leader, or something else — what's important is that you've been accountable for deciding what to build and whether it worked.

  • You have deep, hands-on experience with mobile user acquisition—either directly managing and optimizing acquisition for mobile apps, or building products and infrastructure used by mobile acquisition teams. You understand how app developers actually acquire users, measure performance, and make decisions about where to spend their next dollar.

  • You understand the modern mobile acquisition stack, including MMPs and attribution, Apple Ads, Meta and Google advertising products, conversion APIs, and related measurement infrastructure.

  • You can reason clearly about attribution, performance-marketing economics, and privacy. You understand concepts such as CAC, LTV, ROAS, optimization signals, ATT, SKAdNetwork/AdAttributionKit, consent management, and how downstream behavior should influence acquisition decisions.

  • You thrive in zero-to-one environments. You can take a large, ambiguous opportunity, identify the most important unanswered questions, narrow it into product bets, and find pragmatic ways to test those bets before making large investments.

  • You are sufficiently technical to work closely with engineering on integrations, APIs, SDKs, data flows, identity, attribution, and other technical product decisions.

  • You communicate clearly across different audiences and media, particularly in writing.

In the first month, you'll:

  • Spend significant time with developers understanding how they acquire users today, how they evaluate acquisition performance, and where the process is painful, expensive, fragmented, or opaque.

  • Build a deep understanding of RevenueCat's existing acquisition-related products, integrations, data, customer research, and technical capabilities.

  • Build strong working relationships with engineering, design, data, go-to-market, and other product teams whose work intersects with user acquisition.

  • Develop a clear picture of the acquisition ecosystem, the problems RevenueCat is particularly well positioned to solve, and the biggest assumptions we still need to test.

  • Begin forming your own point of view on where RevenueCat could create differentiated value in user acquisition.

Within the first 3 months, you'll:

  • Have narrowed the broad user acquisition opportunity into a small number of concrete product hypotheses, grounded in customer research, market understanding, and RevenueCat's unique advantages.

  • Have a clear recommendation for where we should focus first — and why.

  • Begin validating that direction through prototypes, design partners, technical exploration, lightweight product experiments, or an initial shippable bet.

  • Establish a learning agenda that makes the biggest risks and unanswered questions explicit, and gives us a fast path to increasing or decreasing our conviction.

  • Align senior stakeholders around what we're testing, what we're not pursuing yet, and what evidence would cause us to change direction.

Within the first 6 months, you'll:

  • Have shipped our first substantive user acquisition product bet, or generated enough evidence to decisively change or stop it before making a larger investment.

  • Have real evidence from the market about where RevenueCat can — and cannot — create differentiated value.

  • Be independently driving product discovery, prioritization, and execution for the user acquisition area.

  • Have developed an evidence-backed point of view on the most promising opportunities in the space and what capabilities RevenueCat would need to pursue them.

  • Have turned a broad strategic opportunity into an increasingly focused product direction.

Within the first 12 months, you'll:

  • Have established a clear strategic direction for RevenueCat in user acquisition, supported by customer behavior and product evidence rather than thesis alone.

  • Have shipped meaningful products or experiments that either created measurable value for developers or materially changed our understanding of the opportunity—including changing or killing bets when the evidence didn’t support them.

  • Have a credible longer-term roadmap for turning the strongest early signals into a meaningful RevenueCat product area.

  • Be the primary IC product owner for User Acquisition and the internal domain expert on how app developers acquire, measure, and optimize users.

  • Have helped define how RevenueCat's monetization data, developer footprint, and advertising capabilities can work together to create a differentiated position in app growth.

What we offer:

  • 10-year window to exercise vested equity options

  • 4-5 weeks of flexible time off annually

  • Workspace budget and continuous learning stipend

Interviewing at RevenueCat

Our interview process is rigorous on purpose. We want to be sure that everyone we bring on is genuinely excited about this work, aligned with how we operate, and ready to meet our high bar for performance. Curious what that actually looks like? Read more in our blog post on how we hire at RevenueCat, including tips to help you succeed.

jobs.jd_full:

About Our Company

Kanopi Studios is a Design, Development & Support Agency with a fully distributed team of experts in Drupal & WordPress.

Our clients are mission-driven - and so are we. We design, build, and support websites that help their missions thrive.

We believe the people behind the work matter just as much as the work itself. That’s why we’re deeply committed to supporting our team’s growth, well-being, and success. When our people thrive, our clients do too - and together, we build a web that works better for everyone.

As Kanopi continues to grow, we’re excited to welcome a new Senior Website Project Manager to our team.

About the Job

We're looking for a process-driven Senior Website Project Manager who brings structure and strategic oversight to every phase of a project and sets the standard for how our project management team works. This role focuses on managing the systems, workflows, and communications that keep client-facing Drupal and/or WordPress projects moving forward, ensuring clarity across teams, maintaining accurate project tracking, and continuously seeking opportunities to improve and streamline how we deliver high-quality digital work.

As a Senior Website Project Manager at Kanopi Studios, you'll guide a mix of Drupal and/or WordPress build and support projects from kickoff through completion, including some of our largest and most complex accounts. You're a client advocate and a strategic partner, and the problem-solver the team counts on when things get complicated. You'll collaborate with cross-functional teams of UX/UI designers, developers, and strategists to ensure each project delivers quality, value, and a bit of Kanopi magic.

This senior-level role requires someone with extensive agency experience leading Drupal and/or WordPress projects. You bring a deep understanding of project life cycles, the judgment to flex between build initiatives and nimble support sprints, and the confidence to guide and mentor other project managers.

Requirements

As a Senior Website Project Manager, your typical day may include:

Client & Project Leadership

  • Manage a portfolio of projects across the build and support spectrum, including high-visibility accounts with complex technical and client needs.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact and trusted advisor for clients, ensuring smooth communication and exceptional service delivery.
  • Understand each client's business needs and effectively communicate them to the internal team to ensure alignment.
  • Know when to push back on behalf of Kanopi's best interests, when to escalate situations to Management, and how to resolve most issues independently before they reach that point.
  • Proactively identify opportunities for larger projects and initiatives, and bring clear recommendations to the Management team.
  • Gain a deep understanding of the client websites you manage so you can proactively recommend improvements.
  • Lead client communications with clarity and empathy, facilitating meetings, demonstrating new features, articulating next steps, sharing updates, and translating technical concepts into plain language.
  • Build positive, long-lasting relationships that encourage contract renewals and account growth.

Planning & Execution

  • Lead project and client onboarding, kickoff calls, and transitions between build and support.
  • Curate and maintain organized, prioritized backlogs that keep project teams focused and work moving forward.
  • Critically evaluate tasks and client requests for strategic fit with client goals and project scope, recommending alternatives when needed.
  • Personally handle "quick win" Drupal and/or WordPress site configurations, content entry, and initial bug troubleshooting before escalating to the development team.
  • Collaborate with clients and internal teams to resolve blockers and anticipate needs.
  • Forecast and coordinate internal resources, including front-end and back-end developers, UX/UI designers, and strategists, based on timing, scope, and expertise.

Quality, Budget, and Timeline Oversight

  • Review completed work (designs, tickets, content, and development) to ensure it meets Kanopi's quality standards before client handoff.
  • Monitor and forecast budgets and timelines to ensure tasks are completed on time and within scope, while providing regular updates to clients and Kanopi management on hours used and project progress.
  • Flag risks early and lead the team in resolving and mitigating issues.
  • Expedite urgent requests, triage issues quickly, and manage escalations, particularly within support accounts.

Tools & Team Collaboration

  • Use tools like Teamwork, Slack, Google Workspace, Zoom, and Claude to stay organized and maintain transparency.
  • Use AI tools like Claude to speed up everyday project work, such as drafting client communications, summarizing meetings, writing tickets, and preparing status updates, while reviewing everything for accuracy before it goes out.
  • Participate in and help lead team meetings, standups, retrospectives, and collaborative discussions that drive ongoing process improvements and a positive team culture.
  • Monitor team workloads and pacing to help maintain a sustainable, healthy balance, identifying early signs of strain or burnout in yourself and others and proactively adjusting priorities when needed.
  • Build and document repeatable processes that improve project success and team satisfaction.
  • Mentor and support other project managers, sharing best practices and serving as a go-to resource for the PM team.

About the Compensation and Work Requirements

This is a full-time position. The starting salary for this role will fall within the range of $75,400.00 - $93,668.00. This range reflects the full good-faith range we reasonably expect to pay for this role across all eligible locations; where you fall within it will depend on your experience and skills, in alignment with current members of our team in similar roles.

This is a 100% remote role. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the US or Canada and be available for regular collaboration during Pacific Time Zone business hours. We are not able to provide visa sponsorship for this position.

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled.

Now, let's talk about you!

We are looking for candidates who…

  • Have 5+ years of digital agency project management experience, including leading Drupal and/or WordPress projects.
  • Have a proven track record managing the full life cycle of web build projects, as well as long-term client support engagements.
  • Are fluent in agile workflows, ticketing systems, and client documentation, and can help teams stay focused and aligned.
  • Are proficient with AI tools like Claude and use them regularly to improve how you plan, communicate, and manage projects.
  • Have hands-on experience troubleshooting bugs, working with site configurations, and managing content in Drupal and/or WordPress.
  • Have a strong working knowledge of best practices in website performance, configuration, and development fundamentals.
  • Know how to balance scope, timelines, and budgets without compromising quality or team morale.
  • Have excellent time management skills to stay on top of your own workload and that of the team members you manage.
  • Have experience forecasting and resourcing development project needs, and understand how to match the right roles to project requirements.
  • Can set clear priorities, communicate shifts effectively, and keep both internal teams and clients in sync.
  • Are proactive, empathetic and confident communicators who listen deeply, explain clearly, and follow through consistently.
  • Stay organized and calm while managing multiple active projects, keeping attention to detail and communication steady as priorities shift.
  • Bring a proactive, solution-oriented mindset to day-to-day delivery, risk mitigation, issue tracking, change management, and escalations.
  • Possess strong problem-solving skills, emotional intelligence, and initiative, and genuinely enjoy helping others succeed.
  • Have experience mentoring or guiding other project managers or team members.
  • Have a passion for the web, for open source software like Drupal and WordPress, and for working with a bunch of fun, thoughtful people.
  • Have experience managing and working with distributed project teams and thrive in a remote-first, collaborative environment.
  • Are available to work during core Pacific Time Zone hours.

Statkraft is Europe’s largest generator of renewable energy from hydro, wind and solar power. We have 6,000 employees in 20 countries. We have been making clean energy possible for over 130 years, with unrivalled expertise in supplying the world with what it needs most. We envision a world that runs entirely on renewable energy.

Because in the fight against climate change, we do not see renewable energy as part of the solution – we believe it must be the solution.

With us, you will shape a career that is truly forward-facing with many amazing opportunities and offerings to match.

We are currently looking for an experienced and enthusiastic Project Manager to join our team in Statkraft UK. The person will report into the Principal Project in the Solar Team. Our offices in the UK are in London, Glasgow and Cardiff. We work on a “hybrid work” mode (3 days office / 2 days work from home) with regular travel within UK and occasionally travel abroad for this position.

Job Description

  • Be responsible for developing ~ 1- 2 projects.
  • Project management of our UK solar pipeline at all stages of project development from site identification through to pre-construction activity,
  • Responsibility for management of project budgets and schedules from early-stage development to point of construction.
  • Managing external service providers including Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and planning consultants, land agents, legal advisors and technical experts;
  • Responsible for obtaining pre commencement planning condition discharge and further investigations as required;
  • Responsible for obtaining any post consent planning variations;
  • Identification of new solar projects, contributing to the development pipeline;
  • Helping manage and coordinate our prospecting efforts for new sites
  • Engage and negotiate agreements with landowners and representatives;
  • Regular reporting on project progress, providing insightful risk and opportunity analysis to management;
  • Stakeholder management (internal and external) and community engagement;
  • Preparing and coordinating internal decision gate documentation.
  • Engagement with the team and developing an understanding of the market.
  • Engage with legal, land, compliance, health and safety, commercial, grid connection and engineering colleagues to integrate these specialisms in your projects;
  • Coordinating with financial and technical colleagues to determine optimal strategy for the project with consideration of project risks;
  • Support development and implementation of solar, energy storage and hydrogen projects as appropriate to the location;
  • Analysing the market for solar energy and contributing to the strategy of the UK Solar Development Team

Qualifications

  • Master or Bachelor degree (or equivalent) in relevant subject e.g. renewables, engineering, planning or environmental and sustainability studies.
  • Experience in the energy (or relevant) industry with a demonstrable track record of successfully achieving targets. Entry level will be determined by experience.
  • Independent self-starter, with attention to detail with the ability to manage a variable workload to key deadlines, often providing support to processes managed by colleagues.
  • Excellent written, fluent English, with presentation and communication skills.
  • Highly proficient in MS Word, Excel and other MS applications.

A career with Statkraft is a career filled with purpose – meaning that every employee is not just making a living, they are making a real difference to the planet, our communities, and the future.   • Professional and personal development in an exciting global company
  • A working environment characterized by competence, responsibility, innovation and a strong commercial culture
  • A diverse workplace with regards to gender, age and cultural background
  • Competitive terms of employment and benefit schemes
  • Career and learning opportunities at various levels of the organisation
  • The chance to grow your career alongside a truly global network of experts, leaders, specialists and graduates from different countries and background

Statkraft’s vision is to renew the way the world is powered. To navigate the complex journey ahead, we need every voice at the table. We therefore work actively to be a diverse and inclusive workplace and welcome all applicants regardless of background, gender, age, sexual orientation, religious belief, ethnicity, nationality or disability.

Description

Project Manager - Onboarding

Location: London
Contract: FTC / Contract (likely 12-18 months)

This senior role leads a large-scale distributor onboarding and data transformation programme, migrating and uplifting around 3,000 distributor records and files into a new strategic platform.

The successful candidate will coordinate across Operations, Distribution, Compliance, Technology, Data Management and external vendors, overseeing offshore delivery teams and keeping senior stakeholders informed. We’re looking for 5+ years of financial services transformation experience, with strong data migration, vendor management and stakeholder skills.

Requirements

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end delivery of the distributor onboarding data migration project.
  • Manage the transfer, validation, cleansing, and uplift of approximately 3,000 distributor records/files into a new strategic system.
  • Coordinate activities across Operations, Distribution, Compliance, Technology, Data Management, and external vendors.
  • Oversee offshore/vendor teams (including eClerx) performing onboarding and data remediation activities.
  • Define project plans, milestones, dependencies, risks, and governance frameworks.
  • Track programme progress and provide regular updates to senior stakeholders.
  • Manage RAID logs, issue resolution, and escalation processes.
  • Drive process improvements and identify opportunities to improve onboarding efficiency.
  • Ensure all onboarding activities comply with relevant regulatory and control requirements.
  • Support User Acceptance Testing (UAT), data validation, and post-implementation activities.

Required Experience

  • Experience delivering business change, onboarding, data migration, or operational transformation projects within Financial Services.
  • Strong experience managing large-scale onboarding, KYC, client lifecycle management, distributor onboarding, fund operations, or asset management transformation initiatives.
  • Proven track record leading cross-functional projects involving Operations and Technology teams.

  • Experience with data migration, data governance, and data quality programmes.
  • Excellent project governance, reporting, and risk management capabilities.

Delta Capita is an equal opportunity employer. We positively encourage applications from suitably qualified and eligible candidates regardless of age, colour, disability, national origin, ancestry, race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, veteran status, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable law.

Most of our clients now require a minimum of 3 days per week in the office, 2 days from home, and accordingly this is also the minimum expectation that Delta Capita require. However, some of our clients have now moved up to 4 days and even 5 days in the office and we require candidates to be flexible to meet our client demands.

Our mission is to reinvent the financial services value chain providing technology-based mutualised services for financial institutions for non-differentiating services.

IQ-EQ is a global investor services group with deep expertise in private markets. We support investment managers, asset owners and global businesses with the administration, compliance, governance, data and reporting that their structures depend on.

Across 25 jurisdictions, our 6,500+ professionals combine technical strength, connected technology and human understanding – the IQ and the EQ – to free clients from operational complexity and give them the peace of mind to focus on their core business activities.

    • Globally distributed teams
    • Fast-paced and rapidly evolving environment

  • Experience of managing third party vendor implementations

As a forward-looking business, sustainability is integral to our strategy and operations. Nium provides global infrastructure for real-time cross-border payments. We were founded on the mission to deliver the global payments infrastructure of tomorrow, today. Our platform enables banks, fintechs, and global businesses to move money instantly, everywhere.   

Co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore with offices in 14 markets worldwide, we are entering one of the most exciting chapters in our journey. In March 2026, we delivered the largest month in our 11-year history with record revenue, record volumes, and EBITDA profitability. Today, Nium moves nearly $60B in payments annually, almost entirely for enterprises, while continuing to strengthen an already healthy balance sheet.  

It is an incredible time to join us, and we are only just getting started.  

Our payout network spans 190+ countries and 100 currencies, with 100 + corridors in real time. We power seamless transfers to accounts, wallets, and cards, support local collections in 35 markets, and as a principal card issuer on Visa, Mastercard, Discover, and UATP, Nium issues over 50 million card tokens every year. Backed by regulatory licenses in 40+ markets, we make it simple for our partners to onboard, integrate, and scale globally. This scale and innovation have earned us recognition as one of CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025, winner of Best Cross-Border Payments Solution at the PayTech Awards, and inclusion in FXC Intelligence’s Top 100 Cross-Border Payments Companies list.  

In 2024, we raised US$50 million in Series E funding at a US$1.4 billion valuation to accelerate network expansion, product innovation, and talent growth. With the B2B payments market projected to hit US$175 trillion by 2030, Nium offers ambitious builders the chance to shape the future of global money movement with the scale of a leader and the energy of a high-growth company. 

Responsibilities

  • Own stablecoin-funded card products — physical and virtual cards funded from or settled in stablecoins (USDC and equivalents). Define the product, get it through compliance, ship it.
  • Build digital asset support into Nium’s multi-currency wallet — hold, convert, and send stablecoins alongside fiat currencies. This is a wallet extension, not a new product line.
  • Design and ship on/off-ramp flows — fiat-to-digital and digital-to-fiat conversion, including rate logic, settlement timing, and failure handling. Own the full customer experience.
  • Drive stablecoin-based cross-border settlement — payin and payout flows that clear on digital rails. Work with network and settlement teams to make these production-grade.
  • Evaluate and integrate custodians, exchanges, and blockchain infrastructure — as infrastructure decisions with integration timelines and SLAs, not as partnership strategy.
  • Own compliance product design for digital assets — MiCA, VASP frameworks, travel rule, FinCEN requirements. These get built into the product spec, not handed off to legal.

Requirements

  • 7+ years in product management. Fintech, crypto infrastructure, or payments required.
  • You’ve shipped at least one digital asset product in production — a stablecoin wallet, a crypto card, an on/off-ramp, or a digital settlement rail. Not a prototype. Not a strategy deck.
  • Strong payments foundation — cross-border flows, FX, wallets, settlement mechanics. Digital assets are an extension of this, not a departure from it.
  • Regulatory fluency as a product skill — you know what MiCA, travel rule, VASP registration, and FinCEN MSB requirements mean for your spec, your launch sequence, and your go/no-go decisions.
  • Experience working with custodians, blockchain infrastructure, or card networks — enough to evaluate integration tradeoffs and write requirements that engineering can build against.
  • Comfortable operating in high-ambiguity, high-compliance environments — you know when to move and when to wait for legal sign-off.

How We’ll Measure Success

  • Volume settled on digital rails (stablecoin payins + payouts) — tracked quarterly against target
  • Card activation rate and spend volume for stablecoin-funded card products
  • On/off-ramp conversion rate and time-to-settlement
  • Time-to-integration for new custodian or blockchain network partners
  • Regulatory coverage: number of markets with compliant, live digital asset product

What we offer at Nium  

 

We Value Performance: Through competitive salaries, performance bonuses, sales commissions, equity for specific roles and recognition programs, we ensure that all our employees are well rewarded and incentivized for their hard work. 

 

We Care for Our Employees: The wellness of Nium’ers is our #1 priority. We offer medical coverage along with 24⁄7 employee assistance program, generous vacation programs including our discretionary year-end shut down (dependant on company OKRs). We also provide a flexible working hybrid working environment (3 days per week in the office). 

 

We Upskill Ourselves: We are curious, and always want to learn more with a focus on upskilling ourselves. We provide role-specific training, internal workshops, and a learning stipend.

 

We Celebrate Together: We recognize that work is also about creating great relationships with each other. We celebrate together with company-wide social events, team bonding activities, happy hours, team offsites, and much more!  

 

We Thrive with Diversity: Nium is truly a global company, with more than 33 nationalities, based in 18+ countries and more than 10 office locations. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to providing a safe and welcoming environment for everyone.  

 

 

Beware of recruitment scams: Be cautious of individuals impersonating Nium via WhatsApp, social media, email or unofficial websites. Do not respond, share personal or financial information, or make any payments. Nium will never ask candidates to transfer money or cryptocurrency as part of our recruitment process.

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. When a contractor in Brazil gets paid on time, a business in Singapore settles in the right currency, or a payroll platform moves money to 40 countries without a single failure: that’s what a good payments platform looks like from the outside. From the inside, it’s hard decisions about which rails to build on, what reliability means at scale, and how to make a platform handling billions a month behave consistently across markets with completely different rules. 

Nium processes cross-border payments for banks, fintechs, and enterprise platforms across 100+ countries. The Senior PM - Payments Platform owns the rails those payments run on. 

Responsibilities

  • Reliability. Define what “good” looks like for corridor performance, settlement success, and straight-through processing. Set the targets, own them, move them.

  • Corridor and market design. Each market has its own mechanics and failure modes. You translate that into requirements: what the corridor supports, how failure is handled, what go-live looks like, so the products built on top can make promises to customers and keep them.

  • Integration standards. You set the bar for what gets built with correspondent banks, local networks, and processors globally. You decide which integrations are worth doing, weighing partner economics and business impact against build and maintenance cost, and you push the ones that matter through to delivery.

  • Resilience. Design for failure: redundancy, failover, degraded modes. The goal is a platform where a single rail going down doesn’t mean customers feel it.

  • AI and agentic payment flows. This is the frontier. Payments infrastructure today is reactive: something breaks, someone fixes it. We want infrastructure that thinks: routes intelligently, detects degradation before customers feel it, reconciles autonomously, resolves failures without human escalation. Nium wants to be the first payments infrastructure company to make agentic flows core to how money moves. You define what that looks like and build it.

Requirements

  • Payments experience at real scale: high volume, multi-market, genuine accountability when things break. You understand the mechanics (settlement windows, return codes, reconciliation, failure handling) well enough to bring unambiguous requirements.

  • Curious about how payments work across markets. AI-native in how you work. Rigorous about prioritization. Opinionated, not passive: you form a point of view on how a corridor or integration should work, and you push it forward rather than waiting to be told what to build.

  • You push Engineering on trade-offs and bring them along with you, holding ground on what’s right for the corridor and the business without needing positional authority to do it. And above all, you are passionate about the customer outcome at the end of the transaction, not the platform for its own sake.

  • 3-5  years in product management. Payments, fintech, or financial infrastructure is a requirement. Experience with real-time rails (UPI, SEPA, RTP, Pix, or equivalents) is a strong plus.

The Opportunity 

Most payments PMs work on one market, one rail, one product type. Here you work on all of them simultaneously: Asia-Pacific, Americas, Europe, MENA, all with different mechanics and failure modes. The exposure you get in two years compresses what usually takes a decade. 

The team is small, senior, and ambitious. The infrastructure you build will process tens of billions of dollars a month and affect the finances of real people and businesses, including the first generation of payments that run through AI agents rather than human-initiated flows.
